Consult Summary:
- Adult with history of childhood asthma, hay fever, and eczema presents with 2–3 days of wheeze, exertional shortness of breath, and cough; advised increased short-acting bronchodilator use via spacer, start antihistamine, and begin peak flow monitoring with follow-up in 1 week.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing and feeling short of breath.
- Onset/duration: 2–3 days.
- Course: Ongoing; worse with walking/exertion; currently feels well at rest.
- Associated symptoms: Cough without sputum; denies hemoptysis and chest pain. Reports “fever,” but measured temperature was 37°C. No nocturnal awakening reported. Exercise intolerance; difficulty completing sentences “sometimes.” Able to climb stairs.
- Triggers/Context: Possible pollen/allergy or viral illness discussed by clinician.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives/positives):
  - Respiratory: Wheeze, dyspnea on exertion, cough. No hemoptysis, no chest pain.
  - Constitutional: Reports “fever,” but measured 37°C.
  - Sleep: Not woken at night.
  - Activity: Unable to walk to work; working from home/sick leave.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma since childhood; described as “quite bad,” required hospital visits (no ICU). Used inhalers in the past; cannot recall names.
- Atopy: Hay fever and eczema.
- Asthma control history:
  - Patient states they stopped asthma medication 3–4 years ago.
  - Also states they “normally” use salbutamol every few weeks and with exercise. Conflict noted.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); patient reports variable/unclear use.
- No other regular medications reported.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine every 2–3 days.
- Living situation: Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Engineer. Currently working from home or on sick leave due to symptoms.
- Exercise: Usually walks to work; currently unable due to dyspnea.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person exam performed (teleconsultation).
- Vitals: None recorded. Patient-reported temperature: 37°C.

Investigations:
- None performed during consult.
- Devices prescribed: Peak flow meter (to record morning and evening values for 1 week); spacer for inhaler use.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected asthma exacerbation (acute wheeze and exertional dyspnea for 2–3 days; cough; no chest pain; no sputum; no nocturnal symptoms; normal reported temperature)
  - Increase short-acting bronchodilator use: 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially.
  - Prescribe spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate correct technique.
  - Prescribe peak flow meter; record readings morning and evening for the next week.
  - Safety-net: Call back immediately if temperature becomes high or wheezing/shortness of breath worsens.
  - Arrange asthma review in ~1 week to assess control and consider additional medication (e.g., another inhaler) based on symptoms and peak flow diary.
- Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis/hay fever
  - Start a regular antihistamine (over-the-counter; specific agent/dose not documented).
- Issue 3: Asthma long-term management considerations
  - Review adherence and clarify current reliever use at follow-up (conflicting history).
  - Consider need for maintenance therapy after reviewing symptom control and peak flow variability.

General Plan items:
- Pharmacist to teach spacer and peak flow technique at pickup.
- Patient agrees to follow-up and monitoring plan.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No objective vitals (HR, RR, SpO2), no physical exam, no current medication list reconciliation (exact inhaler, dose, and frequency unclear), no vaccination status (e.g., influenza), no peak flow baseline.
- Internal conflicts: Patient states they stopped asthma meds 3–4 years ago yet also reports “normal” use of salbutamol every few weeks and with exercise; reports “fever” but measured 37°C (normal).
- Transcript quality: Occasional interruptions/clarification issues; overall history obtainable but with some ambiguity.
